auxiliary_material: The authors note that the control arm's objective response rate was lower than that reported in the KEYNOTE-426 phase 3 trial, attributing this to differences in histology inclusion and PFS calculation timing. Safety data indicated FMT was well-tolerated with no serious adverse events related to the procedure. Limitations include the small sample size (n=45 for primary analysis), reliance on a single main donor for most aliquots, and lack of antibiotic preconditioning which may have limited engraftment efficiency. The study explicitly states that prior to this, no randomized controlled trials had demonstrated FMT efficacy in mRCC.
outline_action: Use this phase 2a RCT data as the highest level of direct evidence available in the supplied material to illustrate current proof-of-concept efficacy and safety. In the review, categorize this under early-phase clinical evidence and explicitly note the absence of phase III confirmation as a critical evidence gap requiring further investigation. Leverage the mechanistic findings (specific strain associations) to propose biomarkers for future large-scale trials.
remaining_gap: The specific success criterion of identifying a completed, large-scale phase III randomized controlled trial is not met by this material, as the TACITO trial is explicitly defined as a phase 2a study with a relatively small sample size. The question of whether phase III confirmation exists remains unanswered by this text.
useful_material: This study (TACITO trial) is an investigator-initiated, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2a trial evaluating fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) in 45 patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) receiving first-line pembrolizumab plus axitinib. The intervention involved FMT from donors who achieved complete response to ICI, administered via colonoscopy and capsules. While the primary endpoint (12-month progression-free survival rate) was not statistically met (70% vs 41%, P=0.053), the secondary endpoint of median progression-free survival was significantly improved in the donor FMT arm (24.0 months vs 9.0 months, HR=0.50, P=0.035). The study confirmed donor strain engraftment and identified specific microbial strains (e.g., Blautia wexlerae acquisition, Akkermansia massiliensis avoidance) associated with clinical outcomes, providing mechanistic insights into microbiome-ICI interactions.
